boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named Manchester destinations on corridors within the practical driving orbit of Saint Anselm College.

cards.title: Nature trail at Blodget Park
cards.subtitle: Front Street corridor
cards.notes: Use Front Street to reach the park’s nature trail and fishing area. Bring footwear suited to an unpaved outdoor walk and leave time to explore the brookside setting.
cards.short_summary: A city-managed conservation park with a trail and fishing amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: Manchester Parks and Recreation lists Blodget Park / Black Brook on Front Street and identifies a nature trail and fishing as amenities.
cards.source_title: Blodget Park - Black Brook | City of Manchester
cards.access_notes: Outdoor city park; check conditions before visiting.

cards.title: Dorrs Pond at Livingston Park
cards.subtitle: Daniel Webster Highway / Hooksett Road corridor
cards.notes: Head up the Daniel Webster Highway corridor for Livingston Park and its Dorrs Pond facilities. Use the city’s park information to plan around the outdoor amenities available there.
cards.short_summary: A named city park associated with Dorrs Pond and a park bath house.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Manchester lists the Dorrs Pond Skate House and Livingston Bath House at Livingston Park on Daniel Webster Highway North.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public park facilities; seasonal operations may vary.

cards.title: Fields and playground at Stevens Park
cards.subtitle: Mammoth Road corridor
cards.notes: Follow Mammoth Road toward Stevens Park for a stop centered on its sports fields and playground. Check the city’s current field schedule if you intend to use programmed facilities.
cards.short_summary: A neighborhood park documented with athletic fields and a playground.
cards.evidence_claim: Manchester’s parks master plan describes Stevens Park as a sports park with a playground and identifies an entrance at Mammoth Road.
cards.source_title: Greening the City: Manchester Parks and Recreation Master Plan
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park; availability of fields can vary with scheduled use.

cards.title: Golf course on Mammoth Road
cards.subtitle: Mammoth Road corridor
cards.notes: Use Mammoth Road to find the Derryfield golf course. If you want to play, consult the club directly for current tee-time, course-access, and event details before heading out.
cards.short_summary: A named Manchester golf-course destination on Mammoth Road.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Manchester lists Derryfield Country Club at 625 Mammoth Road.
cards.access_notes: Golf and event access may require advance arrangements or payment.

cards.title: Currier collections on Ash Street
cards.subtitle: Ash Street corridor
cards.notes: Take Ash Street to the Currier Museum of Art for its collection galleries and exhibition program. Review the museum’s visitor information for current exhibitions and entry details.
cards.short_summary: Manchester’s art museum, documented by the city’s museum network.
cards.evidence_claim: Manchester Museums identifies the Currier Museum of Art as a Manchester museum destination.
cards.access_notes: Museum admission and hours should be confirmed with the museum before visiting.

cards.title: Research stop on Pine Street
cards.subtitle: Pine Street corridor
cards.notes: Make Pine Street your route to Manchester City Library when you need a public research or reading stop. Check the library calendar and service information before planning a longer visit.
cards.short_summary: A named public library destination in Manchester’s central area.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Manchester lists Carpenter Library at 405 Pine Street among its library buildings.
cards.access_notes: Library services and room access may vary by schedule.

cards.title: Open space on Elm Street
cards.subtitle: Elm Street corridor
cards.notes: Use Elm Street to reach Veterans Memorial Park between Central and Merrimack streets. It works as a quick outdoor pause while visiting nearby downtown cultural destinations.
cards.short_summary: A named city park positioned on the central Elm Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Manchester Parks and Recreation states that Veterans Memorial Park is on Elm Street between Central and Merrimack streets.
cards.source_title: Veterans Memorial Park | City of Manchester
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public park; city permitting rules apply to organized events.

cards.title: Murals just off Elm Street
cards.subtitle: Elm Street corridor, between 836 and 844 Elm Street
cards.notes: Walk the Elm Street corridor to Cat Alley and photograph the painted-brick mural sequence. Enter from the block between The Bookery at 844 Elm and 836 Elm Street.
cards.short_summary: A public pedestrian alley with more than 20 cat-themed murals.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Manchester says Cat Alley has more than 20 murals between The Bookery at 844 Elm Street and 836 Elm Street and is open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Public pedestrian walkway; be considerate of adjacent businesses and pedestrians.

cards.title: Manchester history in the Millyard
cards.subtitle: Commercial Street corridor
cards.notes: Use Commercial Street to approach the Millyard Museum and learn about Manchester’s industrial history. Pair the visit with time to look at the surrounding historic mill district from public areas.
cards.short_summary: A museum in Mill No. 3 focused on Manchester history.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Manchester states that the Millyard Museum is housed in Mill No. 3 and tells Manchester’s story from its earliest inhabitants to the present.
cards.access_notes: Museum admission and exhibit access should be confirmed before travel.

cards.title: Hands-on science in the Millyard
cards.subtitle: Bedford Street corridor
cards.notes: Take Bedford Street into the Millyard for hands-on science exhibits at SEE Science Center. Review the center’s visitor details and any timed programming before choosing a visit date.
cards.short_summary: A Manchester science destination with interactive exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Manchester describes SEE Science Center as providing a hands-on interactive scientific experience for children and families.
cards.access_notes: Exhibit entry may require admission; verify current visitor information.
